patch_description:
The previous program failed validation for multiple fundamental reasons: (1) it returned an empty list `[]` as `column_orderings`, so the evaluator had no valid per-row column orderings; (2) the recursive machinery (`reorder_columns_for_value`, `column_recursion`) accessed rows via `getattr(row, col)`/`hasattr` on namedtuples, which breaks with duplicate/space-containing column names, and mutated cells via `result_df.update(group)` and `group.iloc[...] = ...` assignments that can alter stored values; (3) `recursive_reorder` built a result DataFrame without the `original_index` column then re-assigned columns including a fabricated `original_index` column, corrupting shape and data; (4) the whole approach (grouping by a single "max value", splitting rows in half, discarding columns) does not target the actual objective — character-level Trie prefix reuse over serialized rows.

The fix replaces the broken internals with a correct, bounded construction-selection algorithm while preserving the public `reorder` signature, data, and shape: serialize cells (missing → ""), compute per-column length-weighted repetition scores, build up to three candidate orderings (global frequency-ranked order, an alternate length/frequency tradeoff order, and a bounded conditional partition tree producing per-row orders), score each candidate with the true Trie objective (sum of adjacent LCPs of sorted serialized strings, computed with C-speed binary-search prefix comparisons), and return the best. All original cells are output unchanged; `col_merge` and `one_way_dep` are honored with the existing API semantics.
